title: Measuring and Improving Attentiveness to Partial Inputs with Counterfactuals

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model attentiveness using the Counterfactual Attentiveness Test (CAT), which replaces one part of a paired input (e.g., the premise in NLI, the paragraph in Reading Comprehension, or the image in Visual Question Answering) with a randomly sampled counterpart from another instance. This tests whether the model relies solely on dataset artifacts and partial inputs (like hypothesis-only heuristics) rather than reasoning over the full input.

bias_targets.target: Modality bias (Language bias in Vision-Language models)
bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the performance of multimodal models (like BLIP and ViLT) on partial inputs (text-only vs. image-only) and applying counterfactual perturbations to individual modalities to measure if models disproportionately rely on textual language priors rather than visual grounding.
